newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity jumps on outages, higher natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity jumps on outages, higher natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures jumped Thursday on news of generation unit outages in the U.S. West and higher natural gas prices, industry sources said.
"We're looking at some of these outages, as well as hot weather in the Southwest and higher San Juan gas prices," said one New York-based futures trader.
Southwest electricity prices saw a particular increase, hitting new contract highs on news of the increased gas prices, unit outages and warm weather, the sources said.
As of 1235 EDT, NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures were trading up $3.09 at $35.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $36.25 and trade as low as $35.10 per MWh.
August PV was trading up $2.54 at $36.10 per MWh after hitting a new contract high of $36.25 and trading as low as $35.75 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up $2.35 at $22.45 following exchanges in a range of $22.00-22.90, while August was up $1.52 at $24.50 following trades at $24.25-24.75 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 164 COB and 257 PV contracts had traded as of 1150 EDT.
In generation news, officials at the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in San Clemente, Calif., confirmed reports that its restart would be delayed until July.
The company said the unit would likely return to service around July 10, which is about two weeks later than previously expected. San Onofre 3 was shut April 12 for scheduled refueling.

Also, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico may be out of service for a week after it tripped off-line early Wednesday due to a tube rupture, sources familiar with the unit's operations said Thursday.

Some units shut for unexpected maintenance were scheduled to return to service soon, however, with the 750 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada set to be back on line by 1200 PDT, a spokesman for the plant said.
The unit was shut early Saturday for maintenance.

Also, one of two 750 megawatt (MW) units at the Moss Landing natural gas-fired power plant near Monterey, Calif., was restarted as expected, while the other was rescheduled to start around 1600 PDT Thursday.
The unit had been expected to restart early Thursday, but start-up was delayed by a decision to carry out extra maintenance work, the spokesman said. Both units tripped off-line late Monday night.
The 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was tentatively scheduled to restart next Wednesday or Thursday, pending clearance from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
Separately, natural gas prices were rising, with July NYMEX Henry Hub futures up 5.9 cents at $2.23 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) as of 1225 EDT.
Sources said next-day physical gas in the San Juan basin had risen about four cents Thursday to near $2.09 per mmBtu.

Although most six to 10 day forecasts still showed normal to slightly above normal readings in the West, the National Weather Service revised its earlier outlook calling for warmer than normal temperatures across the region.

The complex was also bolstered by a Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee introduction of a proposal to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan still requires the approval of the WSCC board.
PV open interest for June 18 rose 216 to 7,867, while COB open interest rose 45 to 7,173, NYMEX said.
Sources said July and August PV electricity futures may have reached a peak Thursday at the new contract highs of $36.25, with strong resistance seen at that point.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
